script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 30. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Right now, you're connected to billions of computers worldwide.  A message from Tokyo reaches New York in milliseconds.  The internet is humanity's nervous system—a network of networks that transformed what's possible.

Data crosses the internet in packets—small chunks that may take different routes to the same destination. If one path fails, packets find another. This redundancy was built in—the internet was designed to survive even nuclear war. TCP/IP—Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol—is the internet's universal language.  Every device that uses these protocols can communicate with every other.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Shared standards enable cooperation.  The internet teaches that agreement on rules creates capabilities beyond any individual.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Internet Appreciation - See the Network.

Here's your activity: When you use the internet today, pause to consider: your data is traveling through cables, routers, and servers across the world, following agreed protocols. Billions of dollars of infrastructure, decades of development, standards agreed by committees. All to load a webpage in seconds. This helps you appreciate the infrastructure enabling digital life.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how the internet works can be applied to internet appreciation - see the network. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
